learning_outcomes.text: Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being capable of integrating them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society, and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong study for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and industrial engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Perform assemblies, simulations, and laboratory experiments to verify theoretical results and acquire appropriate practical skills.
Acquire the fundamental knowledge of heat transfer necessary to address other more technological subjects.
Know how to use numerical methods to solve complex heat transfer problems.
Know how to apply heat transfer laws to the analytical resolution of simple cases.
Understand the three basic mechanisms of heat transfer and the laws that govern them.

syllabus_topics: 1.2. Physical mechanisms of heat transfer. Basic equations
1.3. Simultaneous mechanisms of heat transfer: Qualitative energy balance
2.1. General heat conduction equation or diffusion equation
4.2. Velocity boundary layer and thermal boundary layer. Reynolds and Prandtl numbers
4.3. Convective heat transfer coefficient. Nusselt number
4.5. Forces involved in natural convection processes. Grashof number
5. COMBINED HEAT TRANSFER: CONDUCTION AND CONVECTION
5.1. Flat, cylindrical and spherical walls with internal and external convection
5.2. Critical radius of insulation for pipes
6.2. Quantities for the study of radiation
7.3. Complex heat transfer: conduction, convection and radiation
assessment_rules: The evaluation is divided into two independent parts: laboratory (LAB) and theory & problems (TyP). The final grade (NF) is calculated as NF = 84% × TyP + 16% × LAB. To pass the course, a minimum grade of 5 (out of 10) is required for LAB, 4 for TyP, and 5 for NF. In the ordinary call, the highest grade between the progressive and global assessment options for each part will be considered. Any parts not passed with a minimum grade of 5 must be retaken in the extraordinary session, though only approved laboratory parts (LAB ≥ 5) can be carried over to subsequent academic years. All grades are out of 10, and if conditions are not met, a grade may be capped at 4.5.
